newsitem.title: UK: Salomon positive on Polish construction sector.
newsitem.headline: Salomon positive on Polish construction sector.

text.p: Poland's construction sector should benefit from new infrastructure developments in 1997, including the launch later in the year of a highway project to build 2,500 km of roads, Salomon Brothers in London said in a report.
It said the project, with an estimated cost of about $10 billion, was likely to directly benefit Mostostal Warszawa, Elektrim, Exbud and Budimex among Warsaw-listed firms.
Preliminary estimates indicate the project would be completed in 15 years.
Salomon said the increasing number of foreign construction firms entering the market were frequently subcontracting work to local companies and providing the finance lacking in the domestic market.
The report was optimistic on the long-term prospects for the sector despite a continued decline in Polish residential construction.
Many firms were taking advantage of new infrastructure projects, including bridges, multi-level parking lots, shopping centres and production facilities.
"New infrastructure developments also look set to increase in future, contributing to the growth of GDP," the report said.
